input.rationale: Section 13.5 starts correctly (Developments created solely by Corio are owned by Corio, with an assignment from Commerce One) but the proviso strips our ownership of our own interface code whenever Commerce One supports it on an ongoing basis — an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor, which is our walk-away. We have deleted the proviso; Commerce One's ownership of the Software itself under Section 2.8 is untouched, and ongoing support can be addressed by a licence back instead.

input.quote: Commerce One hereby grants to Corio a fee-bearing, perpetual and irrevocable, nonexclusive, nontransferable (except in accordance with Section 14.1 of this Agreement), right and license in the Territory
input.rationale: The grant is perpetual and irrevocable and transferable on an M&A per Section 14.1, which is good, but it runs to Corio alone: our affiliates and the contractors we are expressly permitted to use under Section 14.8 are not covered, with no path to add them. Redline inserts affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf into the hosting grant.
